### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hoboken,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Hoboken had a population of 60,419, with 28,175 households and 12,177 families. The population density was 48,335.2 per square mile (18,662.2/km 2). There were 30,202 housing units at an average density of 24,161.6 per square mile (9,328.8/km 2); 6.7% of housing units were vacant, with a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.6% and a rental vacancy rate of 5.2%.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-113)

The median age was 31.7 years; 15.6% of residents were under the age of 18, 9.8% from 18 to 24, 53.3% from 25 to 44, 15.1% from 45 to 64, and 6.3% who were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 100.8 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 100.1 males.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-112)

100.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.0% lived in rural areas.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DHC-114)

Of the 28,175 households, 20.9% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 33.2% were married-couple households, 25.3% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 30.3% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 34.4% of all households were made up of individuals and 5.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.1 and the average family size was 2.7.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-112)

The percent of those with a bachelor's degree or higher was estimated to be 57.0% of the population.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-115)

The 2016–2020 5-year [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey") estimates show that the median household income was $153,438 (with a margin of error of +/- $9,118). The median family income was $200,132 (+/- $18,994).[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-116) Males had a median income of $100,368 (+/- $5,816) versus $77,081 (+/- $3,810) for females. The median income for those above 16 years old was $86,005 (+/- $2,370).[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-117) Approximately, 2.4% of families and 7.0% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 3.1% of those under the age of 18 and 11.0% of those ages 65 or over.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-119)

12.2% of the population were under the age of 18, 12.1% from 18 to 24, 55.9% from 25 to 44, 13.5% from 45 to 64, and 6.3% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 31.2 years. ### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hoboken,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census"), there were 38,577 people, 19,418 households, and 6,835 families residing in the city. The population density was 30,239.2 inhabitants per square mile (11,675.4/km 2), fourth highest in the nation after neighboring communities of [Guttenberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guttenberg,_New_Jersey "Guttenberg, New Jersey"), [Union City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_City,_New_Jersey "Union City, New Jersey") and [West New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_New_York,_New_Jersey "West New York, New Jersey").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-121) There were 19,915 housing units at an average density of 15,610.7 per square mile (6,027.3/km 2). There were 19,418 households, out of which 11.4% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 23.8% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 9.0% had a female householder with no husband present, and 64.8% were non-families. 41.8% of all households were made up of individuals, and 8.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. In the city the age distribution of the population showed 10.5% under the age of 18, 15.3% from 18 to 24, 51.7% from 25 to 44, 13.5% from 45 to 64, and 9.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median income for a household in the city as of the 2000 census was $62,550, while the median income for a family was $67,500. Males had a median income of $54,870 versus $46,826 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $43,195. 11.0% of the population and 10.0% of families were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"). Out of the total population, 23.6% of those under the age of 18 and 20.7% of those 65 and older were living below the poverty line.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-108)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000SF1-122)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hoboken,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Economy")]

The first centrally air-conditioned public space in the United States was demonstrated at Hoboken Terminal.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-124) The first [Blimpie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blimpie "Blimpie") restaurant opened in 1964 at the corner of Seventh and Washington Streets.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-125)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-126) Hoboken is home to one of the headquarters of publisher [John Wiley & Sons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wiley_&_Sons "John Wiley & Sons"), which moved from Manhattan in 2002.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-127) In 2025, [Unilever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unilever "Unilever") moved its North American headquarters from [Englewood Cliffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Englewood_Cliffs "Englewood Cliffs") to 111,200 sq ft (10,330 m 2) of office space at Waterfront Corporate Center in Hoboken.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoboken,_New_Jersey#cite_note-128)

A 2014 study showed that [Stevens Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevens_Institute_of_Technology "Stevens Institute of Technology") contributed $117 million to Hoboken's economy in 2014, reflecting the university's nearly $100 million payroll for salaries and wages, as well as other goods and services acquired, construction and off-campus spending by students and visitors.
